title: SYSK Live: Back When Ford Pintos Were Flaming Deathtraps
summary: Live recording at the Buckhead Theater in Atlanta of Stuff You Should Know covering the Ford Pinto's fuel tank safety scandal. The hosts open with a benefit-show announcement and charity donation pitches (National Down Syndrome Society and Lifeline Animal Project) plus tour dates. The main story covers Lee Iacocca's push for a subcompact under a two-thousand-pound, two-thousand-dollar limit, the Pinto's rear-impact fuel tank and differential bolts, Mark Dowie's Mother Jones "Pinto Madness" article, secret crash tests and the three unused fixes, the cost-benefit analysis that valued a human life, Ford's delays of FMVSS 301 (rear-impact standard), the Highway Safety Act of 1966, Grimshaw trial verdict, the Indiana reckless homicide charges, the recall, and the Pinto's reputation. Several ad reads and crowd-interaction segments are included.
topics: cost benefit analysis human life value

segments.title: Live show opening, tour dates and charity donations
segments.summary: Hosts announce tour dates including added Denver shows and explain that this Atlanta Buckhead Theater show was a benefit, with proceeds going to the National Down Syndrome Society and Lifeline Animal Project. They give text-donation instructions.

segments.title: Lee Iacocca and the Project Phoenix subcompact
segments.summary: Hosts set the scene in Detroit in the 1960s, describing Lee Iacocca's rise after the Mustang, the threat from small European and Japanese cars, and his push for a subcompact car called Project Phoenix with a two-thousand-pound, two-thousand-dollar limit and a twenty-four month timeline.

segments.title: The Pinto's reputation and rear-impact fires
segments.summary: Hosts describe the Ford Pinto's reputation for bursting into flames in rear-end collisions, cite the Popular Mechanics and Leslie Ball quotes, and discuss the gas tank placed six inches from the rear bumper and the differential bolts nicknamed flaming death bolts.

segments.title: Sponsor break and charity reminder
segments.summary: Hosts remind listeners to donate to the National Down Syndrome Society and Lifeline, then read a sponsor message.

segments.title: Mark Dowie's crash description and the 1977 Mother Jones article
segments.summary: Hosts quote journalist Mark Dowie's description of how a Pinto would fail in a rear crash at around thirty miles per hour and discuss the thirteen-gallon spill rate. They introduce Mother Jones' September-October 1977 article Pinto Madness and the press conference with Ralph Nader.

segments.title: Secret crash tests, unused fixes and internal decisions
segments.summary: Hosts explain that Ford carried out secret crash tests, that eleven of forty tests were run before production, and that three fixes (a plastic baffle, a metal bumper reinforcement, and a rubber fuel bladder) were available but not used. They discuss tooling started before the design was final and engineers' comments about safety and trunk space.

segments.title: Second sponsor break and charity reminder
segments.summary: Hosts repeat the donation reminder and read a sponsor message.

segments.title: 1960s auto regulation, Nader's book and the Highway Safety Act
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the largely unregulated auto industry, Ralph Nader's book Unsafe at Any Speed, and the Highway Safety Act passed by Congress. They cover the cost-benefit analysis approach and the NHTSA valuation of a human life at about two hundred thousand dollars, and the memo Ford used with a rounded figure.

segments.title: FMVSS 301 rear-impact standard and Ford's legal delays
segments.summary: Hosts explain Standard 301 setting a twenty mph rear-impact fuel-leak requirement, Ford's attorneys' strategy of filing arguments to delay the rule for nine years, and the NHTSA's study of car fires. They note the criminal sanctions removed from the Safety Act by lobbyists and the fines of about five to ten thousand dollars.

segments.title: Third sponsor break and crowd banter
segments.summary: Short sponsor read and crowd banter, including a bourbon plug and an extended tangent about a listener's underwear and a story about Civil War reenactors.

segments.title: Lawsuits, accident reconstructionists and the Grimshaw verdict
segments.summary: Hosts describe accident reconstructionists and lawyers bringing suits against Ford, the 1977 Orange County trial in which a jury awarded one hundred twenty-five million dollars to Richard Grimshaw (later reduced to about three and a half million), and a Ford attorney's quote about never going to a jury again.

segments.title: Recall, Indiana homicide charges and the Pinto's legacy
segments.summary: Hosts recount Ford's 1978 recall of about 1.4 million Pintos and Mercury Bobcats, the Indiana prosecutor Michael Constantino's reckless homicide charges against Ford executives after a fatal crash, and a Harvard Law Review estimate of 27 deaths. They conclude the Pinto's reputation was largely a public relations problem and mention Lee Iacocca's later career.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: Hosts give social media, email and website contact details and close the show.
